title: toolcall-safe-decoder-adapter: streaming-safe constraint recovery and regex canonicalization
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Added a decoder adapter to improve streaming stability for tool/function calls with constrained decoding backends. Includes tokenizer-aware regex canonicalization, streaming-framing recovery heuristics, and OpenAI-compat shim integration. Backwards-compatible toggle via config flag.
description: Motivation: Intermittent failures were observed when constrained decoding backends (CFG/grammar, regex) run in streaming mode during function/tool-calls. Failures clustered around three classes: streamed token boundaries splitting JSON/toolcall payloads; tokenizer-specific regex mismatches due to byte/segmentation differences; and poor recovery when a constraint rejects a prefix late in the stream. This PR introduces a DecoderAdapter that mediates between the streaming engine and constraint backends to provide tokenizer-aware regex canonicalization, streaming-framing recovery heuristics, a bounded unroll-and-retry fallback for conflicting constraints, and safer framing to avoid splitting top-level JSON braces across chunks. The adapter is feature gated and opt-in via rbx.config.decoder_adapter.enabled. Checklist: unit tests, integration tests, metrics, docs, feature gate applied.
commits: 3 commits: 1) Add DecoderAdapter core and basic tests (ava/decoder-adapter-init); 2) Integrate adapter into OpenAI-compat streaming shim and add integration harness (ava/adapter-openai-integ); 3) Docs, observability metrics, and perf tweaks (ava/adapter-docs-metrics)
review_thread: Diego raised memory concerns about buffering large prefixes; author responded that adapter uses a soft cap and switches to strict-mode when under memory pressure and added tests. Priya requested transparency when user-provided regexes are rewritten; author added decoder_metrics.rewrites_count and debug logging, and updated docs. Evan flagged a flaky integration test on GPU CI; timing-based assertions were removed in favor of event-driven signals and CI passed on rerun. Merge performed by Priya Nair via squash merge.
ci_history: initial CI run failed due to flaky integration test; fix pushed and CI green on rerun
performance_notes: Benchmarks show a 3-7% token throughput overhead when tokenizer recovery heuristics are enabled; introduced 'strict' vs 'relaxed' modes to tune overhead; adapter defaults off for performance-sensitive workloads.
observability: Added decoder_metrics.adapter_rejections, decoder_metrics.adapter_retries, decoder_metrics.rewrites_count, and decoder_metrics.buffered_chunk_bytes. Logs added at debug level when rewrites occur.
integration: Added a flaky-simulation harness in tests/integration/streaming_constraints_harness.py that simulates mid-token splits, multi-byte UTF-8 boundaries, and delayed constraint rejections. CI runs exercise this harness under varied stream chunk sizes.
release_instructions: Feature is behind rbx.config.decoder_adapter.enabled. To enable in Dedicated/Private deployments set decoder_adapter.enabled=true and choose mode via decoder_adapter.mode (strict|relaxed). Monitor decoder_metrics.* and the buffered_chunk_bytes gauge; a recommended soft_cap of 64KB is the default.
example: examples/toolcall/streaming-safe-demo.py demonstrates safe streaming of a tool call with a JSON payload while a regex constraint and a CFG constraint are active. The example toggles relaxed mode to show lower-overhead operation.
notes: Backwards compatibility: adapter preserves prior semantics when disabled; when enabled it avoids producing invalid JSON on stream splits and surfaces constraint rewrites. Related: builds on ENG-11760 prototype and addresses customer incident SUP-3347.
